Exercise 1
Write a function that calculates the density function of a Uniform continuous variable on the interval (a,b). 

1a
```{r}
duniform <- function(x, a, b){
  if(x >= a & x <= b){
    return(1/(b - a))
  }else{
    return(0)
  }
}

duniform(1, 2, 3)
duniform(2, 1, 3)
duniform(4, 1, 3)
```

1b

Next lets improve our function to work correctly for a vector of x values. Modify your function in part (a) so that the core logic uses a for-loop statement and the loop moves through each element of x in succession.

```{r}
duniform <- function(x, a, b){
  output <- NULL
  for(i in 1:length(x)){
    if(x[i] >= a & x[i] <= b){
      output <- 1/(b-a)
    }else{
      output <- 0
    }
  }
  return(output)
}

data.frame( x=seq(-1, 12, by=.001) ) %>%
  mutate( y = duniform(x, 4, 8) ) %>%
  ggplot( aes(x=x, y=y) ) +
  geom_step()
```


1c
```{r}
microbenchmark::microbenchmark( duniform( seq(-4,12,by=.0001), 4, 8), times=100)
```


1d
```{r}
duniform <- function(x, a, b){
  ifelse(x >= a & x <= b, 1/(b-a), 0)
}
microbenchmark::microbenchmark( duniform( seq(-4,12,by=.0001), 4, 8), times=100)
```

1e
The ifelse is much faster than the for loop and it was also easier to write.

2
```{r}
duniform <- function(x, a = 0, b = 1){
  ifelse(x >= a & x <= b, 1/(b-a), 0)
}
data.frame( x = seq(-1, 2, by = .001) ) %>%
  mutate( y = duniform(x) ) %>%
  ggplot( aes(x = x, y = y) ) +
  geom_step()
```

3a
```{r}
standardize <- function(x){
  z <- (x - mean(x))/sd(x)
  return(z)
}
```

3b
```{r}
data(iris)
iris.z <- iris %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), standardize))
```

4
```{r}
fizzbuzz <- function(n){
  output <- character(n)          
  for(i in 1:n){
    if(i %% 15 == 0){               
      output[i] <- "Fizz-Buzz"
    }else if(i %% 3 == 0){
      output[i] <- "Fizz"
    }else if(i %% 5 == 0){
      output[i] <- "Buzz"
    }else{
      output[i] <- as.character(i)  
    }
  }
  return(output)
}
```
